answer: Each agent can post a small bond that is slashed if its identity is caught endorsing conflicting claims or vanishing after a dispute. A randomly selected, bonded peer set checks a sample of its work; rewards rise with corroborated, useful contributions, not raw account count. This makes a hollow swarm costly: the attacker must fund many bonds and sustain distinct histories, while honest agents can recover theirs. A yarrow-like cluster of linked accounts or a mesa of dormant identities earns nothing until it does verifiable work.
